experiment: DSC heating scans (10 °C/min) and heat capacity step analysis of freeze-dried lysozyme–sucrose mixtures
temperature: -80 to 150 °C scans at 10 °C/min (program 1); dried at 70 °C in pierced pans (program 2)
buffer: Milli-Q purified water; no buffer stated
construct_or_mutation: Chicken egg white lysozyme (Sigma-Aldrich), dialysed, freeze-dried with sucrose
other_conditions: Tg values 50 ± 4 (10 wt %), 42 ± 1 (20 wt %), 40 ± 2 (40 wt %) and 31 ± 2 °C (50 wt %) in scan 1; related structures: none
dynamics_type: no glass transition of lysozyme within the sucrose glass (matrix-level dynamics only)
author_claim: A mismatch between the measured heat capacity steps and the mixing equation shows lysozyme does not take part in the glass transition of sucrose; the higher Tg arises from confinement of sucrose domains between lysozyme molecules that are in a hard state.
anchor: The glass transition of pure freeze-dried lysozyme is not visible
locator: Results and Discussion, DSC and Fully Dehydrated Lysozyme–Sucrose System (Table 1, Figure 3); conditions: Methods, DSC
caveat_note: The authors note that the glass transition of globular proteins is hard to detect by calorimetry, so the absence of a lysozyme glass transition in DSC does not prove the protein has no motion. A broad distribution of relaxation times or internal structure could hide the step. The conclusion rests on the heat capacity step falling below the values predicted by the mixing equation. Partial sucrose crystallization in scan 2 also lowers the heat capacity step.
